etymology: English: the polling lift after a party convention, named for the week it lives in.
effect: Adds five points for a fortnight, and lets everyone in the building call it momentum.
tell: A poll released on the last night of the convention, and a surrogate saying "the map has expanded" before the ballots are printed.
expires: Ten days after the balloons, or the first post-convention poll that disagrees with the first post-convention poll.

confused_with.tell: The bounce is measured in polls and the honeymoan is spent in arguments; both expire on a calendar nobody printed.

senses: The polling lift a party gets from its own convention: four days of unchallenged messaging, a balloon drop, and a sample that is briefly paying attention.

It works because attention is the mechanism, not persuasion. The bounce measures who was watching, so it decays as the audience returns to its habits - which is why the number is real and the meaning is mostly theatrical. Conventions have also stopped being news; the bounce shrank as the broadcast became an infomercial.
example: *"The **convention bounce** put him up six, the coverage called it a reset, and three weeks later the same pollster found the race exactly where it started."*
